name: TinyAGI (fka TinyClaw)
vibe_summary: A multi-agent, multi-team orchestrator aimed at running a 'one person company' with isolated agent workspaces and a slick web office UI. Actively developed with rapid feature churn around its TinyOffice dashboard, task system, and channel integrations.
best_for: Solo founders wanting multiple collaborating agent teams
Users who want a polished web dashboard for agent management
avoid_if: You need a stable, production-ready platform (marked experimental)
You want a lightweight single-agent assistant
You require strong sandboxing guarantees out of the box
openclaw_advantages: Native multi-team orchestration with agent hand-offs and fan-out
Rich TinyOffice web UI with task/project management and live visualizer
One-command install with zero-config first run
openclaw_disadvantages: Experimental stability versus OpenClaw's more mature core
Smaller skills/plugin ecosystem than OpenClaw's registry
Heavier Node.js stack and more moving parts to operate
Docker runs as root, weakening in-container isolation
confidence_summary: Evidence is solid for features and activity (detailed README, frequent recent commits, v0.0.20 release), but community sentiment data is thin with only one tangential Reddit mention and mostly aggregator-digest web results.

overview_markdown:
TinyAGI (formerly TinyClaw) is a TypeScript-based multi-agent orchestrator designed around the 'One Person Company' concept: you run multiple teams of AI agents with specialized roles that collaborate via chain execution and fan-out, each in isolated workspaces. It supports Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex providers (plus any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint), persists sessions in SQLite with an atomic queue, retry logic, and dead-letter management, and runs 24/7 as a daemon or Docker container.

Its standout differentiator versus OpenClaw is the TinyOffice web portal — a browser dashboard with a pixel-office agent visualizer, Linear-style task/project management with comments, team chat rooms, and a control plane for services, providers, pairing, and logs. Recent commits show heavy investment in this UI layer, plus a plugin system for message hooks and event listeners.

Compared to OpenClaw, TinyAGI trades ecosystem maturity for orchestration breadth: it is explicitly experimental, its plugin ecosystem is emerging rather than established, and some operational choices (e.g., running as root in Docker, delegating isolation to gVisor) raise the security bar for self-hosters. It fits users who want a managed multi-agent 'company' experience more than a single local assistant.
